clue.text: Engineer stands motionless and overjoyed

indicators.note: in a down entry, something that stands up is read from bottom to top, so the engineer's abbreviation flips

parts.note: CE is short for civil engineer
static means not moving

explanation.surface: An engineer is so delighted he stands frozen to the spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stands' reads as the engineer's posture, but in a down clue it means read from the bottom upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone ecstatic is in a state of intense delight, a close synonym for overjoyed.

clue.text: Advantage of turning outside broadcast on

indicators.note: something turning faces the other way, so the abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast
taken as written

explanation.surface: A TV producer weighs the benefit of switching on an outside broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the abbreviation turns; 'on' stays as it is and follows it.
explanation.definitionFit: A boon is a blessing or benefit, something that helps you, which matches an advantage.

clue.text: Cross after Princess gets key to extension

parts.note: Princess Anne, the British king's sister
a cross is the letter X
E is a musical key

explanation.surface: An irritable royal is handed the key to the new wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross after Princess' places X after ANNE, and the key E finishes ANNEXE. 'Cross' reads like angry but is the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is a building added on to a main one, an extension in the architectural sense.

clue.text: Reacted strangely and made a fuss

indicators.note: acting strangely means behaving oddly, so the letters come out in an odd new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone overreacted and kicked up a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reacted' is the word to rearrange. To create is informal British for to make a fuss or complain loudly.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to create means to kick up a row or complain angrily, so created means kicked up a scene.

clue.text: Be taking new motorist to station, which is capital

parts.note: taken as written
a learner driver displays an L plate
station in the sense of rank or level

explanation.surface: A driving instructor takes a beginner to the railway station in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' suggests trains but means rank, as in one's station in life.
explanation.definitionFit: Belgrade is the capital city of Serbia, formerly of Yugoslavia.

clue.text: Brian gets sick in church of great splendour

indicators.note: the name gets something put into it, taking it in among its own letters

parts.note: taken as written
ill means sick
CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: Brian is taken ill during a service in a magnificent church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In church' suggests location, but the sickness goes inside the name and the church abbreviation is simply added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Brilliance means dazzling brightness or magnificence, which is great splendour.

clue.text: Modest tea set needs replacing

parts.note: cha is British slang for tea

indicators.note: pieces that need replacing are put back differently, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A modest household's tea set is worn out and needs a new one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tea set' looks like one item, but tea is CHA and only 'set' is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Chaste means pure and restrained in behaviour, a sense shared with modest.

clue.text: Large glass vessel

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a tall glass for beer or sherry
second meaning: a sailing ship with fore-and-aft rigging

explanation.walkthrough: 'Glass vessel' reads as a single item like a vase, but the word divides into two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: A schooner is both a big drinking glass in pubs and a two-masted sailing ship.

clue.text: Vulgar listener associated with you in former times

parts.note: the ear is what listens
thy is the old form of your

explanation.surface: Someone who listened to you long ago was rather coarse.
explanation.definitionFit: Earthy humour is crude and down to earth, close to vulgar.

clue.text: Famous model in daily paper appears to shock

indicators.note: one thing being in another means it sits inside the newspaper's name

parts.note: The Sun is a British daily tabloid
the Model T Ford, the famous early car

explanation.surface: A celebrity model's appearance in a tabloid causes a sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Famous model' suggests a catwalk star but is the Model T Ford car, so just T inside SUN.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to stagger or daze someone, as a shock does.

clue.text: Preacher leaving set to be distributed

indicators.note: things distributed are spread around, so these letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A departing preacher leaves a set of items to be handed out.
explanation.definitionFit: An evangelist is a person who spreads the Christian gospel by preaching in public.

clue.text: Firm starts trading in fur

indicators.note: one letter put in another word means it sits inside it

parts.note: sable is a valuable dark fur

indicators.note: where a word starts is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of trading

explanation.surface: A company launches into the fur trade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Firm' looks like a business noun, but it is the adjective. T goes inside SABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: Stable means steady and not easily moved, the same as firm in the adjective sense.

clue.text: Beaten for having first ever party in bed!

indicators.note: the bed is having things put inside it, so it wraps round them

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of ever
the Labour Party, a main British political party

explanation.surface: Someone holds their very first party in bed and gets thrashed for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First ever' means just the opening letter of 'ever'; it joins the party inside the bed.
explanation.definitionFit: To belabour is to attack or thrash someone hard, so belaboured means beaten.

clue.text: Inspector returned hatchet to collier

indicators.note: something returned goes back the way it came, so the word for the tool is read backwards

parts.note: a hatchet is a small axe
a collier is a coal miner

explanation.surface: An inspector hands a borrowed hatchet back to a coal miner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Returned' reads as handing the hatchet back, but it means the tool's name is written backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: An examiner is someone who inspects or tests things, so an inspector by another name.

clue.text: Current demand for applause

parts.note: AC is alternating current
to claim is to demand as a right

explanation.surface: A performer currently demands applause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as present-day, but it is electrical current, AC.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public praise and approval, the kind that applause expresses.

clue.text: Inclined to get home before fiancee

parts.note: at home means in
tended means was inclined, as in tended to agree

explanation.surface: Someone means to get home before their fiancée arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inclined to' sounds like 'meaning to', which fits the surface; 'before' places home ahead of the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: One's intended is the person one plans to marry, an old-fashioned word for a fiancée.

clue.text: Repair man requiring first aid during ramble

indicators.note: the man requires something put inside him, so he wraps round it

parts.note: someone who repairs things is a mender

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of aid

explanation.surface: A repairman out on a country walk has an accident and needs first aid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'First aid' looks like medical help, but it means only the A of aid, placed inside MENDER.
explanation.definitionFit: To meander is to wander aimlessly along a winding route, the same as to ramble.

clue.text: Drains once shut as broken

parts.note: ex means former or once

indicators.note: something broken is knocked out of shape, so these letters fall into a new order

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Drains that were once sealed have now cracked open.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drains' looks like a noun for pipes but works as a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To exhaust a supply is to use it up completely, so exhausts and drains are synonymous verbs.

clue.text: Group support after a disappointment

parts.note: a set is a group
to back is to support

explanation.surface: A band rallies round after a disappointing result.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reverse in progress that leaves you let down, a disappointment.

clue.text: Try to get brown buns — hate having to change

indicators.note: words that have to change take a different form, so their letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A baker trying to brown bread rolls hates having to alter the recipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Buns' suggests baking, but the definition is about getting a tan.
explanation.definitionFit: To sunbathe is to lie in the sun deliberately in order to acquire a tan.

clue.text: Not level? That's odd!

definitions.meaning: first meaning: not flat or smooth
second meaning: of a number, not divisible by two

explanation.walkthrough: 'That's odd!' sounds like surprise, but odd here means a number like 3 or 7.
explanation.definitionFit: The word describes a bumpy surface and also numbers that cannot be split into two equal halves.

clue.text: Attend to the boil

parts.note: to see a doctor or a client is to attend them
taken as written

explanation.surface: A cook is told to see to the pot coming to the boil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Attend to' reads as one phrase, but 'to' only links SEE + THE to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Liquid that seethes bubbles and foams as if boiling, so to seethe is to boil.

clue.text: Becoming perverse, Emlyn conceals it

indicators.note: what is concealed is tucked away inside the words in front of it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and most of the name

explanation.surface: A contrary man called Emlyn keeps something to himself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Becoming' looks like a verb, but it is the adjective meaning suitable.
explanation.definitionFit: Becoming behaviour is proper and fitting, and seemly means exactly that.

clue.text: Poor learner, but could describe goods if not satisfied

definitions.text: could describe goods if not satisfied

indicators.note: a poor performance comes out badly formed, so these letters are muddled

parts.note: taken as written, the letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A slow student isn't happy with a purchase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'But' does double duty: its letters are in the mix, so only 'learner' and 'but' are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Shop goods that can be taken back for a refund when a customer is unhappy are called returnable.

clue.text: Left young boy in uniform outside place of entertainment

indicators.note: the boy stands outside, wrapping round the single letter

parts.note: a Cub Scout, a junior scout who wears a uniform
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A uniformed boy is left waiting outside a nightclub.
explanation.walkthrough: CUB goes round L, giving C-L-UB.
explanation.definitionFit: A club, such as a nightclub, is a venue people visit for dancing and entertainment.

clue.text: Reach first clue and ring crossword compiler!

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter, so only that is taken

parts.note: the opening letter of clue
a ring is round, like the letter O
the setter refers to themself

explanation.surface: A solver gets to the first clue and phones the setter for help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crossword compiler' is the setter, who calls themself ME.
explanation.definitionFit: To come to a place or a point is to reach or arrive at it.

clue.text: The Queen always backs respect

indicators.note: going backwards means the combined letters are read from right to left

parts.note: ER, Elizabeth Regina, the late Queen's cipher
ever means always

explanation.surface: Elizabeth II has always supported respect.
explanation.walkthrough: EREVER read backwards gives REVERE.
explanation.definitionFit: To revere someone is to hold them in deep respect or awe, a verb sense of respect.

clue.text: After California, friendship becomes a disaster

parts.note: Cal is an abbreviation for California
amity is friendly relations

explanation.surface: A friendship turns sour once someone moves to California.
explanation.definitionFit: A calamity is a sudden event causing great damage or distress, so a catastrophe or disaster.
